Common questions

Local LLM basics

What is a local LLM?

A local LLM is a language model that runs on your own computer instead of sending every prompt to a hosted AI service. Software such as Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp can run compatible model files locally.

How much VRAM do I need for a local LLM?

It depends on the model size, quantization and context length. Smaller quantized models can fit in a few gigabytes, while larger models may need 16, 24, 48 GB or more. Use the finder above as a starting point rather than a guarantee.

Does more RAM or VRAM make the model smarter?

More memory lets you load larger models or use longer context, but memory by itself does not improve a particular model. Model design, quantization, inference software and hardware all affect the experience.

Are the speed figures benchmarks?

No. Speed ranges in this version are planning estimates based partly on memory bandwidth. Real tokens per second can differ substantially with the inference backend, GPU support, CPU, settings, prompt length and other factors.

Before relying on a result

This is an experimental planning tool. Model memory, context, task-fit and performance figures may be incomplete or wrong, and model licences can change. Check the model publisher and your chosen runtime before making a purchase or relying on a result.
